clue.text: Cool or cold? Wrap woollen cloth around

indicators.note: around tells us the woollen wrap is placed round the letter for cold

parts.note: a plaid is a woollen tartan cloth worn as a wrap
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone feeling chilly wonders whether to put a woollen shawl round themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like part of a question about temperature, but it is the definition, in its sense of calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A placid person is calm and unflustered, which is the cool of a level-headed temperament.

clue.text: Floral decoration over meeting place in city

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
a den is a private room or haunt where people gather

explanation.surface: A garland of flowers is hung above a venue somewhere in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Leiden is a university city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: What could make academia err — all that backslapping?

indicators.note: the clue asks what the letters given could be turned into, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: University staff may make mistakes amid all their mutual congratulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could make' signals rearranging ACADEMIA and ERR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Backslapping is hearty mutual congratulation, the outward sign of comradeship and good fellowship.

clue.text: Decorative stuff in American state pink paper used for an article

indicators.note: the paper takes the place of an article, the letter A

parts.note: Delaware is a US state
the Financial Times, FT, is printed on pink paper

explanation.surface: A US state uses a pink newspaper for a decorative piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used for an article' swaps one A (the indefinite article) in DELAWARE for FT, giving DELFTWARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is decorative tin-glazed pottery from Delft in the Netherlands.

clue.text: It may have only two wheels phaetons are different

definitions.text: It may have only two wheels

indicators.note: the letters of the carriage name are made different, that is, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Phaetons are carriages that differ, some with only two wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn carriage, often with two wheels.

clue.text: Various yachts around one old Black Sea region

indicators.note: the rearranged boat letters go round the one
various suggests the letters taken in a varied order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sailing boats of many kinds cluster near an ancient region by the Black Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges YACHTS to SCYTHA, and 'around' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scythia was the ancient land of the Scythians north of the Black Sea.

clue.text: Son in an American prison — it's somewhere in Colorado

indicators.note: in places the son inside the other pieces

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A
pen is US slang for a penitentiary

explanation.surface: A son is locked up in an American jail somewhere in Colorado.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspen is a ski resort town in Colorado.

clue.text: Building secured but lacking roof

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, which is taken away

parts.note: shut means closed fast, secured

explanation.surface: A building was locked up but has no roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut is a small simple building.

clue.text: Protect page at front of book

indicators.note: the page letter goes before the book word

parts.note: to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: Guard the page at the start of a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is the verb, reserve, not a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to protect it from harm or decay.

clue.text: Badly doing one's own repairs on the outside of mini

indicators.note: the repairs abbreviation wraps round the word for mini

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself, home repairs
mini means small

explanation.surface: Someone does a poor job of fixing their own Mini car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mini' suggests the car, but it means small.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismally means poorly or miserably, a synonym of badly.

clue.text: Woman on drug making a fuss

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the woman after the drug

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman high on drugs causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A pother is a fuss or commotion, used here as the thing being made.

clue.text: Walkers crossing two rivers to find animal

indicators.note: the walkers go across, that is around, the rivers

parts.note: feet are what we walk on
R is the abbreviation for river, so two give RR

explanation.surface: Hikers ford two rivers to find a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walkers' suggests hikers, but it is FEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferret is a small domesticated animal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Fellows of St Ives recently banned?

indicators.note: of links the men to the place they come from, placed after it

parts.note: St Ives is in Huntingdonshire, abbreviated Hunts
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Men from St Ives have lately been barred from something.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives here is the Cambridgeshire town in old Huntingdonshire (Hunts), not the Cornish one; hunting with hounds was banned in Britain in 2004.
explanation.definitionFit: Fox-hunters lost their legal sport when hunting with dogs was banned in England and Wales in 2005.

clue.text: Special seminar the Spanish held on author's last book

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the earlier piece above the last letter
the rearranged letters hold the Spanish article inside them
special suggests the letters made into something out of the ordinary

parts.note: las is a Spanish form of the

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A special seminar in Spain discusses a writer's final book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' gives SIMARNE; 'held' and 'on' look like one phrase but do separate jobs, one containing and one stacking the pieces in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Silas Marner is a novel by George Eliot.

clue.text: Dull, like Schrodinger's cat?

definitions.meaning: in the thought experiment the boxed cat is in both states at once

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means humdrum, and literally describes the cat which is both dead and living.

clue.text: Distance about to be covered by goddess turning tail

indicators.note: the about word sits inside the goddess
the goddess's tail end is turned round, so its final pair swap places

parts.note: Demeter is the Greek goddess of the harvest
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A goddess turns away and covers some distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' makes DEMETRE, its last two letters swapped; 'about' is the Latin circa, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A decametre is a length of ten metres.

clue.text: Reserved places on board for American suits presumably

definitions.text: Reserved places on board for American suits presumably

parts.words: Reserved places on board for American suits presumably
parts.note: naval areas kept for officers, and fancifully packs of cards named after a US coin

explanation.definitionFit: Quarterdecks are the parts of a ship's upper deck reserved for officers.

clue.text: Sack lady's maid

parts.note: Di is a lady's name, so lady's gives Di's
a miss is a young unmarried woman, a maid

explanation.surface: A lady sacks her maid.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone is to sack them from a job.

clue.text: Vestiges of fire at the ends of winter months

definitions.meaning: the glowing remains left after a fire
November and December both end in the same five letters

explanation.definitionFit: Embers are the smouldering remains of a fire, and novEMBER and decEMBER end so.

clue.text: Animals stare — flipping hawk!

parts.note: to gaze is to stare

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, reading it backwards

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Animals stare up at a blasted bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' looks like the bird, but it is the verb to sell; 'flipping' looks like a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazelles are graceful African and Asian antelopes.

clue.text: Ruled pockets may be so filled?

definitions.meaning: marked with straight guidelines, as writing paper
to fill one's pockets is to make money, and pockets also have a cloth inner layer

explanation.definitionFit: Lined paper is ruled, and lining one's pockets means enriching oneself.

clue.text: A script to end the wrong way, creating unpleasant atmosphere

indicators.note: all three pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a script
an aim is an end, a goal

explanation.surface: A screenplay ends badly, souring the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a heavy unpleasant air or atmosphere.

clue.text: Nothing on cross? Soon supplying wooden carving of deity

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the nothing after the cross

parts.note: X is a cross
O, the figure zero, is nothing
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: An idol is carved soon after a cross bearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A xoanon is a primitive wooden image of a god in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Nothing left at home after upheaval

indicators.note: in a down clue, upheaval lifts the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Nothing is left in the house after a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is a plain synonym for zero, the score of nothing at all in a football result.

clue.text: Meant to offer a bit of 'elp, having finished

parts.note: a hint is a bit of help, and dropping the h as in 'elp gives 'int
ended means finished

explanation.surface: A Cockney offers a little help once the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h in 'elp tells you to drop it from HINT too.
explanation.definitionFit: Intended means meant, planned or designed.

clue.text: A daughter bikes around many islands

indicators.note: the bikes word goes round the other letters

parts.note: bikes are cycles

explanation.surface: A girl's bicycles are strewn around a group of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades are a large group of Greek islands in the Aegean.

clue.text: Way to escape wader's foot being crushed by ship

indicators.note: the bird's last letter, its foot, gives way to the ship

parts.note: an egret is a wading bird
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A wading bird's foot is crushed by a ship, so it seeks a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' means the last letter: T of EGRET is replaced by SS.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit, a way out.
